body_markdown:
Forget your golf course lawns and country houses. As a car-meet setting, nothing is grander than a palace’s grounds.


Hampton Court was the home of King Henry VIII, and when he wasn’t hunting deer in the local park, or going through wives at a rate of knots, he would stroll the manicured gardens of this spectacular riverside pad.


Each year, three-quarters of a million people visit the palace to dive into the rather gruesome past of the Tudors, but today it’s enthusiasts of automotive history who are wandering the grounds, sipping champagne.


There are hundreds of cars on display, from the earliest Benz Patent-Motorwagen to the latest hypercars. In fact, there are so many that it would be easy to become royally lost in the gleaming chrome and polished paintwork.


Among them are Aston Martins aplenty, and, with the British firm being one of the select few car companies to have been issued a Royal Warrant, it seems rather appropriate to focus on the most astonishing Astons at the palace.


## 1935 Mark II Sports Saloon


Concours of Elegance


This Bertelli-bodied machine is believed to be the first Aston ever to be painted in the brand’s trademark green. Only when it was being restored was the original color discovered beneath the leather door cards, and the car was returned to its original hue. Its 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine gave credence to the name Sports Saloon, providing not just a top speed of 85 mph, but a magnificent hot rod-style side exhaust.


## 1961 DB4 GT Zagato


Concours of Elegance


The first, and in many eyes the greatest, collaboration between Aston Martin and Italian coachbuilder Zagato was on the DB4 GT. Ercole Spada took on the design duties, sculpting a glorious, organic shape that also happened to save over 90 pounds of weight. This 1961 car is one of just four built and was raced by Roy Salvadori, Jim Clark, and Stirling Moss. No wonder it’s one of the[most valuable Aston Martins ever made](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/the-most-expensive-aston-martins-ever-sold-at-auction/) , with its sister car selling for more than $13M in 2018.


## A Zagato Trio

In 2017, Aston Martin handed over the Vanquish to its Italian partners. The plan was to build 99 Vanquish Zagato Coupes (above left) and the same number of Shooting Brakes (above right). There were also to be 99 Volantes and 28 Speedsters, all underpinned by the Vanquish S platform, with its 5.9-liter V-12 and Touchtronic III automatic transmission. Handsome cars, for sure, but neither stands out quite like the 1990 V8 Vantage Zagato with its array of awesome angles. This car has been completely restored, or “reactivated” as[seller Nicholas Mee](https://www.nicholasmee.co.uk/aston-martin-car-sales/21484644-aston-martin-v8-vantage-zagato-reactivated/) prefers. Even though it had only covered 600 miles since new, the Vantage has, nonetheless, been “extensively re-commissioned” with “all original components removed, or replaced, and added minor but effective updates to improve the car’s usability and durability.”


## 1983 Lagonda


Concours of Elegance


It may have been Aston Martin’s biggest folly, but this 1983 Lagonda proved popular with the judges and was given the Best Car Club Award. Could it have been William Towns’ (very straight) lines that swayed them? Or perhaps it was the car’s over-complex solid-state electronics or built-in television and drinks cabinet? No wonder[each car took 2200 man-hours to construct](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/aston-martins-outlandish-lagonda-turns-50/) and Aston Martin lost money on every one made.


## Oscar Indias


Concours of Elegance


Before you ask, yes, there were some DB5s, but they’re not on my list so that I could make room for my all-time favorite Aston Martin. The Oscar India, which got its name from its October Introduction in 1978, is just such a handsome beast. It ripples with muscle, but is more Statham than Schwarzenegger in the way it fills its suit without bursting from the seams. There were a few examples on show, such as this V8 Vantage which had traveled from California for the occasion.


## 2012 One 77


Concours of Elegance


Quite rightly hailed as a Future Classic winner, the Aston Martin One 77 was hailed at its launch as the company’s fastest-ever road car. Its top speed was 220 mph, and it would reach 60 mph from rest in a tire-frying 3.7 seconds, courtesy of its naturally aspirated, 750-hp, 7.3-liter V-12 mounted up front. The One 77 was relatively light, deploying a carbon fiber monocoque over which its hand-beaten body panels were draped. Only 77 were built, each priced at a cool one million pounds.
